questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of secure, auditable deployments and basic rollback mechanics in CodePipeline.

## Key Concepts
- Least-privilege IAM for Lambda execution role and CodePipeline
- API Gateway permissions and resource policies
- CloudWatch alarms and automatic rollback in CI/CD
- Versioning and rollback of Lambda functions

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  LambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: "lambda.amazonaws.com" }
            Action: "sts:AssumeRole"
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: LambdaLoggingPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: "arn:aws:logs:*:*:*"
        - PolicyName: S3AccessPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: s3:GetObject
                Resource: "arn:aws:s3:::deployment-bucket/*"

  LambdaFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Role: !GetAtt LambdaRole.Arn
      # ... other function properties

  ErrorAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: LambdaErrorAlarm
      AlarmDescription: "Triggers rollback on 5xx errors"
      MetricName: 5XXError
      Namespace: AWS/ApiGateway
      Statistic: Sum
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 5
      Threshold: 10
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref RollbackAction

  RollbackAction:
    Type: AWS::CodePipeline::Action
    Properties:
      Configuration:
        ActionTypeId:
          Category: Invoke
          Owner: AWS
          Provider: Lambda
          Version: 1
      InputArtifacts: []
      Name: RollbackAction
      RunOrder: 2
```

## Testing Steps
1. Deploy the CloudFormation stack
2. Verify Lambda has only minimal IAM permissions
3. Test API Gateway access controls
4. Trigger 5xx errors to confirm CloudWatch alarm activation
5. Verify automatic rollback to previous Lambda version

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests release governance, least-privilege principles, and practical DevOps automation in AWS. It also evaluates the ability to translate business requirements into concrete infrastructure changes.

## Key Concepts
- CodePipeline stages and manual approval actions
- Stage-specific artifact storage using separate S3 buckets
- IAM role scoping for production deployments with guardrails

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  ProdPipeline:
    Type: AWS::CodePipeline::Pipeline
    Properties:
      RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CodePipelineServiceRole
      Stages:
        - Name: Source
          Actions:
            - Name: Source
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Source
                Owner: ThirdParty
                Provider: GitHub
              Configuration:
                Owner: my-org
                Repo: my-repo
                Branch: main
              OutputArtifacts:
                - Name: SourceOutput
        
        - Name: Build
          Actions:
            - Name: Build
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Build
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CodeBuild
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: SourceOutput
              OutputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildOutput
              Configuration:
                ProjectName: MyBuildProject
        
        - Name: Deploy-Staging
          Actions:
            - Name: DeployStaging
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Deploy
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CloudFormation
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildOutput
              Configuration:
                StackName: my-app-staging
                TemplatePath: BuildOutput::template.yaml
                RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CodePipelineDeployRole
              
        - Name: Manual-Approval
          Actions:
            - Name: ApproveProdDeploy
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Approval
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: Manual
              Configuration:
                CustomData: "Please review and approve production deployment"
        
        - Name: Deploy-Production
          Actions:
            - Name: DeployProduction
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Deploy
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CloudFormation
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildOutput
              Configuration:
                StackName: my-app-prod
                TemplatePath: BuildOutput::template.yaml
                RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CodePipelineProdRole
      ArtifactStore:
        Type: S3
        Location: !Ref ProductionArtifactsBucket
  
  StagingArtifactsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: my-app-staging-artifacts
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
  
  ProductionArtifactsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: my-app-production-artifacts
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
  
  CodePipelineProdRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: CodePipelineProdRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: codepipeline.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSCodePipelineFullAccess
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ProductionDeployOnly
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cloudformation:CreateStack
                  - cloudformation:UpdateStack
                  - cloudformation:DeleteStack
                  - cloudformation:DescribeStacks
                Resource: arn:aws:cloudformation:*:*:stack/my-app-prod/*
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:PutObject
                  - s3:ListBucket
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt ProductionArtifactsBucket.Arn
                  - !Sub "${ProductionArtifactsBucket}/*"
              - Effect: Deny
                Action:
                  - cloudformation:CreateStack
                  - cloudformation:UpdateStack
                Resource: arn:aws:cloudformation:*:*:stack/my-app-staging/*
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical CI/CD implementation across GitHub, CodePipeline, CloudFormation, and ECS Fargate, emphasizing real-world patterns like feature flag management via AWS AppConfig and automated health-based rollback mechanisms.

## Key Concepts
- AWS AppConfig hosted configurations for dynamic feature flag management
- ECS Fargate deployment orchestration using CloudFormation
- CodePipeline integration with CodeBuild for automated testing
- Health-check monitoring and automated rollback for safe deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
# CloudFormation snippet (simplified) for AppConfig and ECS
Resources:
  MyAppConfigApplication:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Application
    Properties:
      Name: my-microservice-config
      Description: Feature flag configuration for microservice

  FeatureFlagEnvironment:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Environment
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref MyAppConfigApplication
      Name: production
      Description: Production environment configuration

  FeatureFlagProfile:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::ConfigurationProfile
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref MyAppConfigApplication
      Name: feature-flags
      LocationUri: 'hosted-configuration'

  FeatureFlags:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::HostedConfigurationVersion
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref MyAppConfigApplication
      ConfigurationProfileId: !Ref FeatureFlagProfile
      Description: Feature flag configuration
      Content: |
        {
          "featureXEnabled": false,
          "featureYEnabled": true
        }
      ContentType: 'application/json'

  ECSService:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    Properties:
      Cluster: !Ref MyCluster
      TaskDefinition: !Ref MyTaskDefinition
      DesiredCount: 2
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          SecurityGroups: [!Ref MySecurityGroup]
          Subnets: [!Ref PrivateSubnet1, !Ref PrivateSubnet2]
          AssignPublicIp: DISABLED
      LoadBalancers:
        - ContainerName: my-app
          ContainerPort: 8080
          TargetGroupArn: !Ref MyTargetGroup
      HealthCheckGracePeriodSeconds: 60

  MyTargetGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
    Properties:
      Port: 80
      Protocol: HTTP
      VpcId: !Ref MyVPC
      HealthCheckPath: /health
      HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 30
      HealthCheckTimeoutSeconds: 5
      HealthyThresholdCount: 2
      UnhealthyThresholdCount: 3
```

## Testing Steps
1. **Setup Phase**: Create AppConfig application and environment, deploy initial CloudFormation stack
2. **Feature Flag Testing**: Verify endpoint is gated when featureXEnabled=false, enable flag and confirm endpoint accessibility
3. **Health Check Validation**: Test health endpoint responds correctly, simulate 5xx errors to trigger rollback
4. **End-to-End Pipeline**: Commit code changes, validate CodePipeline executes build, test, and deploy stages successfully
5. **Rollback Verification**: Enable problematic feature flag, confirm automated rollback triggers when health checks fail

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  ReleaseNotesTopic:
    Type: AWS::SNS::Topic
    Properties:
      DisplayName: ReleaseNotes
  ReleaseNotesLambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ReleaseNotesPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 'sns:Publish'
                Resource: !Ref ReleaseNotesTopic
  ReleaseNotesFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Handler: index.handler
      Runtime: python3.9
      Role: !GetAtt ReleaseNotesLambdaRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK: "https://hooks.slack.com/services/REPLACE/WEBHOOK"
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json, os, urllib.request
          def handler(event, context):
              webhook = os.environ['SLACK_WEBHOOK']
              payload = json.dumps({'text': f"Deploy {event.get('app','app')}:{event.get('tag','latest')} by {event.get('commit','')} - {event.get('pr','')}"})
              req = urllib.request.Request(webhook, data=payload.encode(), headers={'Content-Type':'application/json'})
              urllib.request.urlopen(req)
```

## Code Example

```yaml
# FIS experiment manifest skeleton
apiVersion: aws FIS/v1
kind: Experiment
metadata:
  name: dr-chaos-test
  region: us-east-1
spec:
  description: "Cross-region DR chaos experiment"
  tags:
    approved: "true"
    environment: "dr-test"
  targets:
    msk-replication:
      resourceType: "aws:msk:cluster"
      selector:
        clusterArn: "arn:aws:msk:us-east-1:123456789012:cluster/shared-cluster"
    eks-workloads:
      resourceType: "aws:eks:pod"
      selector:
        clusterName: "eks-primary"
  actions:
    pause-replication:
      actionId: "aws:msk:pause-replication"
      parameters:
        duration: "60s"
    steer-traffic:
      actionId: "aws:eks:interrupt-pod"
      parameters:
        mode: "random"
        percentage: "50"
```
